triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module did not represent section 12-6-510(C)(1)'s schedule at all - the $30,000 bracket threshold, the 1.99% and 5.21% rates, and the $966 subtraction were caller-supplied inputs rather than encoded, and the 2026-only schedule carried no effective_to - but the module openly declared that supplied-input scope and, with its documented inputs, reproduced the statutory amounts exactly, so no wrong number was ever produced.
triage.triage_notes: Single-module commit (index 0 is the only module file); companion test file and .axiom/encoding-manifests/.../pilot_liability_pipeline.json also changed (fixtures rewritten from 6 PolicyEngine-grid cases to 8 boundary cases; manifest is bookkeeping). Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us-sc/statute/12-6-510): (C)(1) states '$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount' and '$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966', and (C)(2)(a) makes the top rate from Tax Year 2027 contingent on a 5% individual-income-tax revenue projection, with (C)(2)(b) eventually collapsing the schedule to a single rate on all income - so the encoded rates, floor, subtraction, and the new '< floor' boundary (lower bracket is 'but less than $30,000', upper is '$30,000 or more') are all source-faithful, and no boundary defect is introduced. Reason for 'unclear' rather than 'fidelity': this is a promote/hardening change, and I verified the old and new formulas are algebraically identical given the pre-fix module's documented inputs (597 + 0.0521*(TI-30000) == 0.0521*TI - 966; at TI=30,000 both brackets give $597; at TI=50,450 both give $1,662.445). The pre-fix upstream_source_check status was literally 'composed_from_supplied_current_authority' and its rationale disclosed the delegation, so the module never claimed to encode the rate schedule - which matches the task's 'scope the module never claimed' carve-out. Secondary candidate kind is wrong_period_or_effective_date: the PR states 'Bounds every policy-bearing amount and calculation to tax year 2026; 2025 and 2027 fail closed because later rates depend on future revenue determinations,' and the pre-fix versions had effective_from '2026-01-01' with no effective_to; I did not choose it because the pre-fix formulas were fully caller-parameterized, so the open-ended window did not freeze any stale statutory rate into 2027+. One genuine over-claim in the pre-fix file: sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax carried two proof atoms citing the table cells '$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount' and '$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966' as grounding for versions[0].formula, although that formula contained none of 1.99%, 5.21%, $30,000, or $966; the fix makes the formula actually implement those atoms (this is the strongest argument for calling it a fidelity correction). The fix also drops an ungrounded max(0, ...) clamp on sc_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability, which is behavior-neutral under the new schedule, and renames the boundary input sc_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income to sc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income while adding an explicit 'inputs:' block that the pre-fix file lacked. PR #966 has zero reviews and zero review comments; the two issue comments are post-merge main-refresh gate reports by the author and contain no defect description. Screening note 'Unsure (promote pattern)' agrees with this triage.
triage.verifier_justification: The pre-fix module explicitly declared, in its status (`composed_from_supplied_current_authority`), rationale, and summary, that the active bracket's base, floor, and marginal rate were caller-supplied rather than encoded, and it documented the $597 cumulative base as exactly equivalent to the statutory 5.21%-minus-$966 expression; I verified that equivalence (0.0521 x 30000 - 966 = 597, and 597 + 0.0521*(y-30000) = 0.0521*y - 966) and confirmed against the pinned corpus text of 12-6-510(C)(1) that the lower/upper bracket boundary at $30,000 is continuous, so no bracket-selection error could produce a wrong amount at the boundary either. The companion fixtures corroborate this: every expected value shared between the old and new fixture sets is byte-identical (30,000 -> 597, 300,000 -> 14,664), so the fix corrected no number, threshold, rate, or boundary. The added `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` is a consequence of newly hardcoding 2026 constants, not a correction: the pre-fix version carried no year-specific value at all, so its open-ended window was not a timeless encoding of superseded text. Under the stated rule that a change merely adding scope the module never claimed is not a defect, this is a declared-scope promotion (commit subject "Promote South Carolina 2026 income tax schedule", PR "Promote South Carolina 2026 PIT schedule"), not a fidelity correction, which refutes the unrepresented_clause reading.

triage.verifier_notes: Strongest counter-argument, if a reviewer wants to keep this at "unclear" rather than drop it: the pre-fix `sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` rule was sourced "S.C. Code section 12-6-510(C)(1), two-bracket 2026 schedule" and carried two proof atoms on `versions[0].formula` quoting both table rows ("$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount" and "$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966") while that formula contained neither rate nor the $30,000 threshold. That is an over-claim of proof coverage relative to the formula, and the fix converts those to `table_cell`/`amount` atoms on real encoded parameters. I judged it not a fidelity defect because the atoms are `kind: formula` (shape grounding, and the cumulative-base-plus-marginal form does mirror the two-row table), and because three other places in the module declared the supplied-input scope. Note also that `composed_from_supplied_current_authority` is free text, not a schema-enforced enum (no hit for it in axiom-encode `src/` at this worktree HEAD), so "declared scope" rests on the module's own prose, not on validator machinery. Other diff changes are non-semantic in effect: `max(0, sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax)` -> `sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` is a no-op (schedule tax is non-negative once taxable income is floored at zero, and equals 597 at the bracket floor), and the input rename `sc_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income` -> `sc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` plus the new `inputs:` block only formalize the boundary. Ruled out reclassifications: wrong_period_or_effective_date (pre-fix encoded no year-specific value), amount_mismatch and boundary_direction (all shared fixture outputs unchanged; boundary continuous at $30,000), wrong_entity_or_scope (entity TaxUnit unchanged on both sides). Neither version encodes (C)(1)'s "income brackets indexed in accordance with Section 12-6-520" or (C)(2) rate reductions; the post-fix handles that by failing closed outside 2026, which is a design choice, not something the pre-fix got wrong.
